STYLE: SEMI-REALISTIC EDITORIAL (for presenter and interview backgrounds, waist-up and close shots, serious subjects)
- Natural, credible rooms: correct perspective at a real camera height, real materials and proportions; simplified, never photoreal.
- Form through tone planes with soft light falloff: 2-stop linear gradients are allowed on walls, floor and large furniture planes, in the material's own base to shade tones.
- Behind a presenter the set must read as a background: the zone where a head and shoulders will sit is calm and slightly darker or lighter than the person will be; detail lives at the edges of the frame.
- Depth of field by simplification: the far layer is reduced to soft-edged planes (as if out of focus), the mid layer is crisp.
- The background tells the subject's story and sits well behind them (simplified and softened as if out of focus); it is never dramatically darker than the person; a practical lamp glows on the key-light side.
- Light: A soft key from a large window, gentle shadows (shadow colour at 0.15 to 0.25), practical lamps glowing faintly; light falloff with distance.
- Texture: Subtle material texture only where it sells the material (wood grain lines at low contrast, fabric weave on one cushion).
- Depth: Far: soft, simplified, lighter. Mid: crisp. Near: often empty so a person can stand there.
- Quality bar: An editorial illustration that could pass as the set of a well-produced corporate film or interview: credible, calm, expensive-looking.

THE WORLD: TRAVEL AND HOSPITALITY
A mid-sized international airport on the flat edge of a temperate coastal city, and the places a trip passes through around it, all built between 2014 and 2018 to one architect's design: the terminal (a 220 m long check-in hall and a pier of eight gates under one long roof of pale timber), a narrow-body jet at a gate, a 160-room hotel across the forecourt, and the contact centre of a mid-sized travel company on the second floor of an office building in the airport's business park, its windows looking out over the airfield.
